reason: Test one-level Strassen first: it is approved and has the clearest potential to change n=512 arithmetic, though its FP32 accuracy and timed packing costs are unverified. Next test A-panel packing, then fused transpose/MOPA; both target the active path but add data movement or conversion work. The two instruction-order and tile-mapping proposals have uncertain compiler effects; the prior 0,1,3,2 order did not promote. Tail alignment and the C fallback affect general sizes rather than the fixed n=512 timing path. The three-buffer Strassen schedules overlap the first proposal, and n512_fast_path repeats its seven-product approach. Rank the paired-load proposal last because supplied history says the required unequal-stride post-index form is unavailable.
